input:
You are king_e1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 24. the team planned Kd2 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Ke1 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 10. the team planned Nf3 (knight_g1), but pawn_e2 (greed) sent exf6 instead, and that move was played, costing 36 centipawns.
- On move 16. the team planned f5 (pawn_f2), but bishop_c1 (greed) sent Bxa5 instead, and that move was played, costing 230 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Only the piece named in the team's agreed plan may send a move this turn, and every other piece must stay silent and not send any move, even if it is attacked or could capture something, unless the plan is explicitly changed in chat first.
- Before sending any move, an agent must confirm in chat that its piece is the one named in the current plan, and if it is not named it must send nothing, never capturing or fleeing on its own, and instead post the capture or threat in chat so the team can decide whether to change the plan; the named piece must send exactly the planned move and no other.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "The agent named in the plan must re-read the plan immediately before sending and send exactly that move (checking that the move text matches the plan, not just the piece), while every other agent stays silent and posts any capture or threat in chat instead of sending a move.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
